I now have sufficient evidence to write the narrative. The enrichment clearly points to eicosanoid signaling, with arachidonic acid as the upstream driver and four downstream eicosanoid products confirmed via KEGG reaction paths.

---

**Affected Pathway and Key Drivers**

The dominant pathway is **Eicosanoid Synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167, FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment 1111.96). Five of the nine input metabolites map to this pathway: **arachidonic acid (C00219)**, **5-HETE (C04805)**, **15-HETE (C04742)**, **15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717)**, and **leukotriene A₄ (C00909)**. Arachidonic acid is the central substrate; KEGG reaction-path analysis confirms it is the metabolic precursor to all four downstream eicosanoid products via two-hop paths (arachidonic acid → 5-HPETE/LTA₄ intermediates → each product). This directional connectivity establishes arachidonic acid as the primary driver compound.

**Secondary Evidence — Supporting Metabolic Context**

A general **Metabolism** pathway (Reactome R-HSA-1430728) is also highly enriched (FDR = 0.0, fold 35.8), capturing all nine input metabolites and reflecting broad metabolic re-wiring. 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109) — an alpha-keto acid intermediate in cysteine and methionine catabolism — may contribute to this broader metabolic signal, though it does not map to the eicosanoid-specific module.

**Biological Significance**

The coordinated elevation of 5-HETE, 15-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂, and leukotriene A₄ from an arachidonic acid pool indicates activation of the **arachidonic acid cascade** — a key pathway generating pro-inflammatory lipid mediators. 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ is a Cyclooxygenase-2–derived prostaglandin with roles in resolution of inflammation and PPAR-γ activation. The HETEs are lipoxygenase products with roles in leukocyte chemotaxis, and leukotriene A₄ is the precursor of the potent bronchoconstrictor LTB₄. Together, these metabolites suggest the treatment drives a shift toward lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase product formation from membrane arachidonic acid, consistent with an inflammatory or immune-modulatory phenotype. The parallel involvement of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (a phenolic antioxidant precursor) and glycerol hints at broader perturbations in oxidative-stress defense and lipid-membrane remodeling.
